uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: ECOLOGY What is Ecology? Ecology is the scientific study of the way that living organisms interact with each other and their environment. The word “ecology” comes from the Greek words ‘oikos’, meaning “house” and ‘logos’, meaning “logic” or “knowledge.” To fully understand the science of ecology, there are some common terms that must be defined. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: ECOLOGY Habitats A habitat is a place where a plant or animal lives. Habitats provide a place where organisms can find food, shelter and reproduce. One example of a habitat is a harbour. A harbour provides shelter, food and a place to reproduce for fish, shellfish, stingrays and even whales. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: ECOLOGY Adaptations Every organism has certain features, behaviours or characteristics that allow it to live successfully in its habitat. These features are called adaptations and we say that the organism is adapted to its habitat. Organisms living in different habitats need different adaptations.
